discovery: Optical detection and coherent control of single solid-state spins (nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond), enabling quantum sensing and quantum networks
subfield: Quantum physics / solid-state spin qubits and quantum sensing
motivation: Wrachtrup and Jelezko first optically detected magnetic resonance of a single defect spin in diamond and demonstrated coherent control and readout of individual electron and nuclear spins at room temperature. This turned a fragile quantum degree of freedom in a solid into a measurable, controllable qubit. Lukin, together with Wrachtrup, established the nitrogen-vacancy center as an atomic-scale magnetometer and showed spin-photon entanglement and nuclear-spin quantum memories, which form the basis of solid-state quantum networks. Their work opened an entire field. Nanoscale NMR, imaging of magnetism and currents in condensed matter, biological sensing, and loophole-free Bell tests all rest on this platform, and so do the many new defect qubits that followed in silicon carbide and other hosts. It is a rare case of deep quantum physics becoming a broadly adopted measurement technology.
